pruning_window: Pollard at start of dry season; can re-pollard mid-year
notes: Fast nitrogen-fixer, the classic high-shade service tree over coffee and cacao. Pollarded hard for biomass / chop-and-drop. Returns sun to the system on demand.

pruning_window: Formative pruning only, dry season
notes: Valued straight-grained timber that self-prunes. Light, open crown lets understory crops keep producing — common emergent in shaded cacao.

pruning_window: Formative pruning only, dry season
notes: High-value aromatic timber, long rotation. The long-term capital of the system. Watch for shoot borer (Hypsipyla) when grown in the open.

pruning_window: Pollard 1-2x per year, into the dry season
notes: The workhorse of syntropic systems. Fast nitrogen-fixer, heavy biomass for chop-and-drop, edible sweet pulp. Coppices vigorously after hard pruning.

pruning_window: After harvest; thin to keep light in the canopy
notes: Reliable high-value fruit across the highlands. Surface-rooted, so keep a thick mulch layer and avoid disturbing soil beneath it.

pruning_window: Just after fruiting, before the next flush
notes: Anchor fruit tree for the dry tropics; a dry spell triggers flowering. Prune to open the centre and stagger harvest.

pruning_window: After harvest; remove deadwood and water-shoots
notes: Steady cash fruit with a long harvest window. Benefits from the filtered light of an emergent layer rather than full exposure.

pruning_window: Continuous: de-leaf and de-sucker; fell the stem after harvest
notes: Early income and abundant mulch. Cut pseudostems drop huge biomass back onto the bed. Keep three stems per mat (fruiting / following / sucker).

pruning_window: Light pruning after main harvest; maintain a single low canopy
notes: Shade-loving understory cash crop — needs the high/emergent layers above it. Keep airflow to limit pod diseases (monilia, black pod).

pruning_window: n/a (not pruned; replace every 2-3 years)
notes: Fast pioneer fruit that produces within a year, filling the gap while slower trees establish. Short-lived; plant in succession.

pruning_window: After fruiting; cut back hard to control size and renew wood
notes: Hardy, drought-tolerant fruit that crops young. Can volunteer aggressively, so manage seedlings.

pruning_window: After harvest; stump/renew on a multi-year cycle
notes: The flagship shaded cash crop of the highlands. Performs best under the dappled shade of Inga or Erythrina rather than full sun.

pruning_window: n/a (harvested whole at 8-18 months)
notes: Tough pioneer staple that grows on poor soil and tolerates drought. Stems replant directly. Good early-cycle ground occupant.

pruning_window: Cut back to ~50 cm to rejuvenate; chop-and-drop prunings
notes: Short-lived nitrogen-fixing shrub. Edible pulse, living mulch, and windbreak in one. A core pioneer for restoring degraded ground fast.

pruning_window: n/a (remove offshoots after harvest)
notes: Drought-hardy ground crop that tolerates partial shade. Useful edge and border planting; suckers extend the planting for years.

pruning_window: n/a (trim vines to control spread)
notes: Fast living ground cover that smothers weeds and shades the soil while yielding a staple tuber. Ideal first-cycle floor of the system.

pruning_window: n/a (dies back; lift rhizomes in the dry season)
notes: Shade-tolerant rhizome crop for the deep understory. Thrives in the moist, mulched floor beneath cacao and bananas.

pruning_window: n/a (annual; cut at soil line and leave roots)
notes: Quick nitrogen-fixing annual to interplant between young trees. Climbing types use maize or saplings as support. Leave roots in the ground.

pruning_window: n/a (harvest pads and fruit; remove pads to shape and propagate)
notes: Extremely drought-hardy cactus for the driest ground and exposed edges. Both the young pads (nopales) and the fruit (tuna) are eaten. Pads root where they fall, so it doubles as a living fence. You will suffer greatly for this plant, prepare to have endlessly painful hands, no gloves on earth will save you.

pruning_window: Cut-and-come-again: harvest leaves continuously; coppice to keep within reach
notes: Hardy, fast-regenerating leaf crop grown from cuttings — a Guatemalan staple. Productive for years with almost no care and tolerates drought. Leaves must be cooked before eating (raw leaves contain hydrocyanic compounds).
